Thought: Potassium oxalate (K2C2O4) is a salt of oxalic acid. To determine its flammability, I need to consider its chemical properties. Inorganic salts like potassium oxalate are generally noncombustible because they are already in an oxidized state. Unlike organic compounds that can readily oxidize in combustion reactions, inorganic salts like potassium oxalate typically don't burn. They may decompose at high temperatures, but they don't sustain combustion on their own. This is a characteristic property of many metal salts.
Final Answer: Potassium oxalate is an inorganic salt that doesn't readily burn or support combustion. As with many metal salts, it is already in an oxidized state and therefore doesn't undergo combustion reactions like organic compounds do.
